key_insight: A proposed type-I photonic fusion gate reaches 5/8 (62.5%) direct success using just two independent ancillary photons, matching a prior four-photon scheme with half the ancilla.
engineering_relevance: Lower ancillary-photon demand and fixed output modes could simplify resource-efficient photonic quantum computing hardware.
method: Use two independent single-photon ancillas without entangled ancillary input.
Combine predominantly passive optics with one detection-controlled phase-shift or mode-swap element.
Keep successful outputs in fixed modes, avoiding conditional output routing.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved robustness to heralded ancillary-photon loss and more than 4.6% lower average single-photon consumption for six-qubit ring graph generation versus other type-I schemes.
watch_item: The abstract presents a proposed design rather than an experimental demonstration; detection-conditioned active control remains an implementation requirement.
paper_title: Minimal ancilla for boosting type-I photonic fusion
